reportedFindings.claim: CFDs are leveraged derivatives; providers need an SC derivatives or CFD-restricted derivatives licence.
reportedFindings.scope: Malaysia / all CFD providers / retail and sophisticated investors
reportedFindings.quote: “Entities who wish to offer CFD will be required to hold either a licence for dealing in derivatives or dealing in derivatives restricted to CFD…”
reportedFindings.limitations: Contributor-reported assessment, not DEVIN FOREX verification or approval. Superseded references and geographic inferences are addressed in the independent source-check report.

reportedFindings.claim: Malaysian CFDs may be offered only to sophisticated investors, not retail investors.
reportedFindings.scope: Malaysia / all CFD providers / ordinary retail residents
reportedFindings.quote: “Currently, CFD can only be traded by sophisticated investors…”
reportedFindings.limitations: Contributor-reported assessment, not DEVIN FOREX verification or approval. Superseded references and geographic inferences are addressed in the independent source-check report.

reportedFindings.claim: The CFD Guidelines expressly prohibit offering CFDs to retail investors.
reportedFindings.scope: Malaysia / all CFD providers / retail investors
reportedFindings.quote: “The (name of CFD) is not allowed to be offered to retail investors.”
reportedFindings.limitations: Contributor-reported assessment, not DEVIN FOREX verification or approval. Superseded references and geographic inferences are addressed in the independent source-check report.

reportedFindings.claim: Malaysian CFDs are limited to qualifying shares and equity indices.
reportedFindings.scope: Malaysia / all CFD providers / sophisticated investors
reportedFindings.quote: “CFD offered in Malaysia are only allowed to be based on shares and indices…”
reportedFindings.limitations: Contributor-reported assessment, not DEVIN FOREX verification or approval. Superseded references and geographic inferences are addressed in the independent source-check report.

reportedFindings.claim: BNM approval may be required based on client residence and CFD currency.
reportedFindings.scope: Malaysia / CFD providers / resident or non-resident clients
reportedFindings.quote: “A CFD provider may require approval from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) depending on their targeted investor types…”
reportedFindings.limitations: Contributor-reported assessment, not DEVIN FOREX verification or approval. Superseded references and geographic inferences are addressed in the independent source-check report.

reportedFindings.claim: A first-time Malaysian CFD investor must be assessed for suitability.
reportedFindings.quote: “A CFD provider must conduct a suitability assessment on an investor who wishes to invest in CFD for the first time in Malaysia.”
reportedFindings.limitations: Contributor-reported assessment, not DEVIN FOREX verification or approval. Superseded references and geographic inferences are addressed in the independent source-check report.

reportedFindings.claim: Residents without domestic MYR borrowing may invest in foreign-currency assets onshore or abroad without an amount limit; this is not CFD-product permission.
reportedFindings.quote: “Residents without domestic MYR borrowing are free to undertake any amount of investment in FCY asset onshore or abroad.”
reportedFindings.limitations: Contributor-reported assessment, not DEVIN FOREX verification or approval. Superseded references and geographic inferences are addressed in the independent source-check report.

brokerResearch.name: Exness

reportedFields.value: **Not established.** Exness’s Malaysia-specific domain and Labuan entity indicate local operational presence, but neither establishes that an Exness entity is authorised to offer retail leveraged forex/CFDs to Malaysian residents under the SC framework.

**Not established for Malaysian retail clients.** Exness discloses multiple international entities, including Exness (SC) Ltd (Seychelles, FSA licence SD025), Exness B.V. (Curaçao, CBCS licence 0003LSI), Exness (VG) Ltd (BVI, FSC licence SIBA/L/20/1133), and Exness Investment Bank Ltd (Labuan, LFSA licence 210141BI).

Broker-stated. Exness lists these licences and says its entities do not serve certain jurisdictions, including the USA, Iran, North Korea, Europe, the UK, Russia and Belarus; Malaysia is not named in the retrieved restriction wording.  [exness](https://www.exness.com/regulation/)

Exness operates `my.exness.com`, and its Labuan entity is located in Labuan, Malaysia. However, its Labuan licence is for Investment Banking Business, not an SC CFD-dealing licence.  [my.exness](https://my.exness.com/cnf/config-pa-en.js)
**No — exclude pending entity/product permission**

unresolvedNotes: No locally authorised Malaysian retail forex/CFD route or serving-entity allocation is established by this packet.

brokerResearch.name: XM

reportedFields.value: **Not established.** XM maintains a Malaysia-localised site and its public restricted-regions notice does not name Malaysia, but omission is not acceptance evidence.

**Not established for Malaysian residents.** XM’s global legal documents identify Trading Point of Financial Instruments Ltd, a Cyprus investment firm regulated by CySEC under licence 120/10, but this does not establish that this Cyprus entity contracts with Malaysian residents.

Broker-stated. XM says it does not serve citizens of the USA, Canada, Israel, Iran “and other sanctioned countries,” and that users must observe local restrictions.  [xm](https://www.xm.com/legal-documents)

XM has a Malaysia-specific research portal at `xm.com/my/`, but this is marketing/localisation evidence, not a contracting-entity or regulatory-permission record.  [xm](https://www.xm.com/my/research-portal)
**No — exclude pending entity/onboarding verification**

legalReviewQuestions: Does Exness identify a specific contracting entity and product permissions for Malaysian retail residents, rather than merely operating a Malaysia-localised site and maintaining a Labuan investment-banking entity?

Does XM identify the exact entity that would contract with a Malaysian resident, and does that entity have a documented permission or legal basis relevant to leveraged forex/CFD services for that resident class?
Does IC Markets identify a Malaysia-specific contracting entity or confirm that IC Markets (EU) Ltd accepts Malaysian retail residents?
Does Pepperstone identify a Malaysia-specific contracting entity or confirm Malaysian retail onboarding?

What are the exact current categories and thresholds in the SC’s Guidelines on Categories of Sophisticated Investors, including whether a “sophisticated investor” can access offshore forex/CFD products and under what conditions?
Does BNM publish a current, directly applicable notice on resident payments or remittances for forex/CFD trading with an offshore broker, beyond the general foreign-currency investment framework?
Are there any current SC enforcement, investor-alert, or unauthorised-entity notices specifically naming Exness, XM, IC Markets, or Pepperstone in relation to Malaysian clients?
